messages.subject: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results
messages.subject_clean: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results
messages.body_plain:
Dear all, dear subread team,

I work with mouse and sometimes human data, and I have a problem concerning the counting of multimapped reads. I want to allow multimapping during the alignment step, because otherwise all genes that are duplicated in the genome will be lost. When I summarize reads with featureCounts at the gene level, I specify -M (countMultiMappingReads), but not -O (allowMultiOverlap). The description of -O states: "If specified, reads (or fragments if -p is specified) will be allowed to be assigned to more than one matched meta-feature". I assumed that without -O, a read would be counted only if it is aligned to the features of exactly one meta-feature. Now, I have the impression that multi-overlaps are rather defined at the level of individual alignments and not individual reads. If a read aligns to more than one place in the genome, each alignment of this read will be evaluated (and counted) separately. Here are two examples:

SRR1029044.282    16    chr12    69159416    1    58M    *    0    0TCGGCATCAATATGGTGACCTCCCGGGAGCGGGGGACCACCAGGTTGCCTAAGGAGGG    DDEFFFFFFFHHHHHHHEJJJJJJJJJIJJJJJJJJJIGJJJIJJHHHHHFFFFFCCC    NH:i:3    HI:i:1    AS:i:57    nM:i:0
SRR1029044.282    0    chr12    69361303    1    58M    *    0    0CCCTCCTTAGGCAACCTGGTGGTCCCCCGCTCCCGGGAGGTCACCATATTGATGCCGA    CCCFFFFFHHHHHJJIJJJGIJJJJJJJJJIJJJJJJJJJEHHHHHHHFFFFFFFEDD    NH:i:3    HI:i:2    AS:i:57    nM:i:0
SRR1029044.282    16    chr6    69516460    1    58M    *    0    0TCGGCATCAATATGGTGACCTCCCGGGAGCGGGGGACCACCAGGTTGCCTAAGGAGGG    DDEFFFFFFFHHHHHHHEJJJJJJJJJIJJJJJJJJJIGJJJIJJHHHHHFFFFFCCC    NH:i:3    HI:i:3    AS:i:57    nM:i:0

SRR1029044.282    Assigned    Rn7s1    Total=1;Votes/Targets=1/2
SRR1029044.282    Assigned    Rn7s2    Total=1;Votes/Targets=1/2
SRR1029044.282    Assigned    Rn7s6    Total=1;Votes/Targets=1/2

The read is designated as "Assigned", although it overlaps more than one meta-feature.
I realized that specifying -M has another unwanted side-effect: If a sequence occurs several times within the same gene, due to tandem repeats, it is counted several times for the same gene:

SRR1029044.655    16    chr4    130935190    0    58M    *    0    0    TGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCCTCCCACCACTCACTGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCAEHEC=A@=@7HF<CGEBED??:3GG?:EA4GHFAFF<+G?ABG@DFBB?DDDAD<<?    NH:i:7    HI:i:2    AS:i:57    nM:i:0

SRR1029044.655    16    chr4    130935262    0    58M    *    0    0    TGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCCTCCCACCACTCACTGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCAEHEC=A@=@7HF<CGEBED??:3GG?:EA4GHFAFF<+G?ABG@DFBB?DDDAD<<?    NH:i:7    HI:i:4    AS:i:57    nM:i:0
SRR1029044.655    16    chr4    130935298    0    58M    *    0    0    TGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCCTCCCACCACTCACTGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCAEHEC=A@=@7HF<CGEBED??:3GG?:EA4GHFAFF<+G?ABG@DFBB?DDDAD<<?    NH:i:7    HI:i:5    AS:i:57    nM:i:0
SRR1029044.655    16    chr4    130935334    0    58M    *    0    0    TGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCCTCCCACCACTCACTGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCAEHEC=A@=@7HF<CGEBED??:3GG?:EA4GHFAFF<+G?ABG@DFBB?DDDAD<<?    NH:i:7    HI:i:6    AS:i:57    nM:i:0
SRR1029044.655    16    chr4    130935370    0    58M    *    0    0    TGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCCTCCCACCACTCACTGCAGTGCTCACCATGGAGCCCAEHEC=A@=@7HF<CGEBED??:3GG?:EA4GHFAFF<+G?ABG@DFBB?DDDAD<<?    NH:i:7    HI:i:7    AS:i:57    nM:i:0

SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1
SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1
SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1
SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1
SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1
SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1
SRR1029044.655    Assigned    Laptm5    Total=1

If a gene occurs several times in the genome, the gtf file that is provided by the user might contain this gene more than once, and I guess that the read aligning to this gene will be counted as many times as the gene occurs, if -M is specified. I can't check this in my data, because my gtf contains each gene only once.

I think, the user guide might be a bit clearer here if it stated explicitly that multi-overlaps are defined individually for each alignment of a read in the case of -M. And perhaps it might be a nice addition to featureCounts in the future to perform the assignment to genes at the level of reads and not individual alignments?

Best wishes,

Johanna

messages.subject_clean: ~90% mapped but not assigned more than 20%?
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I am a newbie user of Subjunc and featureCounts. I need to pass our data soon to my PI and I am seeing something that is a bit concenring: all my libraries get mapped more than 90% in subjunc but they don't get assigned more than 20% in featureCounts. I have tried -s 0 -s 1 -s 2. So I would not think it's strand thing. Also I have used the normal gtf file and dna primary assembly.fa file.

These are the files I used for building the index, aligning, and counting:

Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.dna.primary_assembly.fa

Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.86.gtf

I have attached the summary of featureCounts.

Thank you very much your help and ideas are very appreciated,

Aref

messages.subject: Re: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results
messages.subject_clean: countMultiMappingReads without allowMultiOverlap gives unexpected results
messages.body_plain:
Hi Johanna,

You are correct that the counting of multi-mapping reads is performed at the level of individual alignments when '-M' is specified. I will make this more clearer in the users guide.

You are also correct that a read mapping to a repetitive gene in the genome will be counted multiple times, when '-M' is specified.

Have you looked at the '--fraction' argument? With this argument, each alignment from a multi-mapping read will get a fractional count, which makes the alignment counting be equivalent to read counting if all alignments are counted.

Best wishes,

Wei

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I'm just running an old pipeline on a new server with a newer version of subread (v1.5.0-p1). My old pipline specified the -H flag but I cannot see any documentation of -H in this version of subread? Has it been depreciated or is it on by default now? When I call subread it lists 'Hamming distance : yes'.
Best,
Peter
